formulas: A relation R from A to B is a subset of A × B.
Function: every element of A has exactly one image in B.
Invertible function: f is bijective ⇒ f⁻¹ exists.
Number of relations from A to B = 2^(m×n), where |A|=m, |B|=n
Number of functions from A to B = n^m
Number of one-one functions = nPm (if n≥m)
Number of onto functions from A to B (|A|=m, |B|=n) = Σ(-1)^k · nCk · (n-k)^m
derivations: Prove: If f: A→B and g: B→C are one-one, then gof is one-one.
Proof: Let x₁, x₂ ∈ A such that (gof)(x₁) = (gof)(x₂). ⇒ g(f(x₁)) = g(f(x₂)). Since g is one-one, f(x₁) = f(x₂). Since f is one-one, x₁ = x₂. Hence gof is one-one.
Prove: If f and g are onto, then gof is onto.
Proof: Let z ∈ C. Since g is onto, ∃ y ∈ B with g(y) = z. Since f is onto, ∃ x ∈ A with f(x) = y. Then (gof)(x) = g(f(x)) = g(y) = z. Hence gof is onto.
Prove: If f and g are bijective, then gof is bijective.
Proof: From above two results, gof is both one-one and onto. Hence bijective.

Proof: Let f: A→B and g: B→C be bijective. Then gof: A→C is bijective. (gof)⁻¹: C→A. Also g⁻¹of⁻¹: C→A. For any x ∈ A, (gof)(x) = g(f(x)). Let y = f(x), z = g(y). Then (gof)⁻¹(z) = x. Also (g⁻¹of⁻¹)(z) = g⁻¹(f⁻¹(z)) = g⁻¹(y) = x. Hence (gof)⁻¹ = g⁻¹of⁻¹.
pyq: Q1 (2023): Let f: R→R be defined by f(x) = 2x + 3. Find f⁻¹. — Ans: f⁻¹(x) = (x-3)/2
Q2 (2022): Show that f: R→R, f(x) = x³ is bijective. — Ans: One-one: f(x₁)=f(x₂) ⇒ x₁³=x₂³ ⇒ x₁=x₂. Onto: For y∈R, x=y^(1/3)∈R, f(x)=y. Hence bijective.
Q3 (2020): If f(x) = x² and g(x) = x+1, find fog and gof. — Ans: fog(x) = (x+1)², gof(x) = x²+1
Q4 (2019): Number of one-one functions from set A with 3 elements to set B with 4 elements. — Ans: ⁴P₃ = 24
Q5 (2018): Prove that the relation R = {(a,b): a ≤ b} on R is reflexive, transitive but not symmetric. — Ans: Reflexive: a≤a ✓. Transitive: a≤b, b≤c ⇒ a≤c ✓. Not symmetric: 2≤3 but 3≰2 ✗.
Q7 (2022): Let A = {1,2,3}, B = {4,5}. Find number of functions from A to B. — Ans: n^m = 2³ = 8
Q8 (2021): Check if f: R→R, f(x) = x² is one-one. — Ans: f(1)=1, f(-1)=1, but 1≠-1. So not one-one.
Q10 (2019): Find the number of relations from A={a,b} to B={1,2,3}. — Ans: 2^(2×3) = 2⁶ = 64
Q11 (2023): Prove that f: R→R, f(x) = 5x+3 is bijective. — Ans: One-one: 5x₁+3=5x₂+3 ⇒ x₁=x₂. Onto: For y∈R, x=(y-3)/5∈R, f(x)=y. Hence bijective.
Q12 (2022): If f: R→R, f(x) = x²+1, find f⁻¹(5). — Ans: x²+1=5 ⇒ x²=4 ⇒ x=±2. Since f is not one-one, f⁻¹(5) is not unique. If we restrict domain to [0,∞), f⁻¹(5)=2.
Q14 (2020): If A has 3 elements and B has 2 elements, find number of onto functions from A to B. — Ans: Σ(-1)^k · ²Ck · (2-k)³ = 2³ - 2·1³ + 0 = 8-2 = 6
Q15 (2019): Show that R = {(1,1),(2,2),(1,2),(2,3)} on A={1,2,3} is not transitive. — Ans: (1,2) and (2,3) present but (1,3) absent. So not transitive.
Q17 (2022): Find number of bijective functions from A to B where |A|=|B|=4. — Ans: 4! = 24

Q19 (2020): Check if R = {(a,b): a divides b} on N is reflexive, symmetric, transitive. — Ans: Reflexive: a divides a ✓. Not symmetric: 2 divides 4 but 4 does not divide 2 ✗. Transitive: a|b, b|c ⇒ a|c ✓.
Q20 (2019): If f(x) = x², g(x) = √x, find (fog)(x) and (gof)(x). — Ans: (fog)(x) = f(√x) = x. (gof)(x) = g(x²) = |x|.
Relations and Functions.notes: Chapter 1: Relations and Functions. Key points: (1) Relation = subset of Cartesian product. (2) Empty relation, Universal relation, Identity relation. (3) A function is a special relation. (4) Types of functions: Identity, Constant, Polynomial, Rational, Modulus, Signum, Greatest Integer. (5) Algebra of functions: (f±g)(x), (f·g)(x), (f/g)(x). (6) Invertible functions only when bijective. (7) Number of relations = 2^(mn). (8) Number of functions = n^m. (9) Number of one-one functions = nPm. (10) Number of onto functions = Σ(-1)^k nCk (n-k)^m.

formulas: Principal value ranges: sin⁻¹: [-π/2, π/2], cos⁻¹: [0, π], tan⁻¹: (-π/2, π/2)
derivations: Proof: Let sin⁻¹x = θ. Then sinθ = x, and cos(π/2 - θ) = sinθ = x. So cos⁻¹x = π/2 - θ. Hence sin⁻¹x + cos⁻¹x = θ + π/2 - θ = π/2.
Proof: Let tan⁻¹x = A, tan⁻¹y = B. Then tanA = x, tanB = y. tan(A+B) = (tanA+tanB)/(1-tanA·tanB) = (x+y)/(1-xy). So A+B = tan⁻¹((x+y)/(1-xy)). Hence tan⁻¹x + tan⁻¹y = tan⁻¹((x+y)/(1-xy)).
Proof: Put y = x in tan⁻¹x + tan⁻¹y formula: 2tan⁻¹x = tan⁻¹((x+x)/(1-x·x)) = tan⁻¹(2x/(1-x²)).
Proof: 3tan⁻¹x = tan⁻¹x + 2tan⁻¹x = tan⁻¹x + tan⁻¹(2x/(1-x²)) = tan⁻¹((x + 2x/(1-x²))/(1 - x·2x/(1-x²))) = tan⁻¹((x(1-x²)+2x)/(1-x²-2x²)) = tan⁻¹((3x-x³)/(1-3x²)).
pyq: Q1 (2023): Find principal value of sin⁻¹(-1/2). — Ans: -π/6
Q4 (2020): Solve tan⁻¹2x + tan⁻¹3x = π/4. — Ans: (2x+3x)/(1-6x²) = 1 ⇒ 5x = 1-6x² ⇒ 6x²+5x-1=0 ⇒ x = 1/6 or x = -1. x = -1 rejected (makes negative). x = 1/6
Q5 (2019): Find sin⁻¹(sin(2π/3)). — Ans: sin⁻¹(sin(2π/3)) = sin⁻¹(√3/2) = π/3 (since 2π/3 ∉ [-π/2,π/2])
Q6 (2023): Find cos⁻¹(cos(7π/6)). — Ans: cos⁻¹(cos(7π/6)) = cos⁻¹(-√3/2) = 5π/6 (since 7π/6 ∉ [0,π])
Q7 (2022): Find principal value of tan⁻¹(-1). — Ans: -π/4
Q9 (2020): Find value of tan⁻¹(1) + tan⁻¹(2) + tan⁻¹(3). — Ans: tan⁻¹(1)+tan⁻¹(2) = tan⁻¹((1+2)/(1-2)) = tan⁻¹(-3) = π - tan⁻¹(3). Then π - tan⁻¹(3) + tan⁻¹(3) = π
Q10 (2019): Solve sin⁻¹x = π/6. — Ans: x = sin(π/6) = 1/2
Q11 (2023): Find value of sin(cos⁻¹(3/5)). — Ans: Let cos⁻¹(3/5) = θ. cosθ = 3/5, sinθ = 4/5. So sin(cos⁻¹(3/5)) = 4/5

Q18 (2021): Solve for x: sin⁻¹x + sin⁻¹(1-x) = cos⁻¹x. — Ans: Let sin⁻¹x = A, sin⁻¹(1-x) = B. sin(A+B) = x·√(1-(1-x)²) + (1-x)·√(1-x²) = cos⁻¹x = π/2 - sin⁻¹x. This is complex. Standard answer: x = 0 or x = 1/2. Verify x=1/2: sin⁻¹(1/2)+sin⁻¹(1/2) = π/6+π/6 = π/3 = cos⁻¹(1/2). ✓
Inverse Trigonometric Functions.notes: Chapter 2: Inverse Trigonometric Functions. Key points: (1) Inverse trig functions are defined only for restricted domains. (2) Principal value branch is the range where function is one-one and onto. (3) Graphs of sin⁻¹x, cos⁻¹x, tan⁻¹x. (4) Properties: sin⁻¹(sinθ) = θ only if θ ∈ [-π/2,π/2]. (5) Important: sin⁻¹x + cos⁻¹x = π/2 for all x ∈ [-1,1]. (6) tan⁻¹x + tan⁻¹y formula with conditions. (7) 2tan⁻¹x and 3tan⁻¹x formulas. (8) Principal value ranges must be remembered.
